definition: A crude BCI implant that transmits signals through the user's skeletal structure rather than dedicated neural pathways, producing a characteristic buzzing sensation in the teeth and jaw during use. Associated with black-market installations and Tier 1 self-modification.
origin: Street cant derived from the physical sensation of vibration through the mandible during transmission
usage: Used by Shelf and lower Old Harbor residents who can't afford legitimate BCI installations; also used as an insult toward anyone with visibly inferior implant work
example: You can always tell a bone radio operator — watch for the jaw clench every time they try to ping someone.
